scope: Bounded local frozen-source review only. No runtime/source modification, remote access, test, compiler, GPU, model, profiling or instrumentation action.
answer: Yes, under enabled expert caching and eligible mixed-residency layers, asynchronously completed swaps can be published at different forward boundaries. Identical total GPU/CPU capacities and seed profile do not prove identical per-expert residency throughout a request.

certainty_levels.source_confirmed: Worker completion queues are sampled without draining all inflight copies at ordinary cache ticks; swaps change expert identity mappings while preserving capacities.
certainty_levels.conditional_mechanism: Different execution/copy scheduling could put a completion on opposite sides of a tick, changing later mapping or inflight admission. A faster new kernel is one possible timing perturbation, not a measured fact in these unmeasured arms.
certainty_levels.unknown_arithmetic: Whether a CPU/GPU execution reassignment changes any result bits for the actual expert inputs is unproven. Separate implementations and reduction grouping do not alone establish inequality.
certainty_levels.unknown_causation: No saved per-expert residency, copy-completion/round timings, or draft IDs/shapes establish this mechanism in N0/N1 before divergence.

necessary_conditions: Expert cache enabled and at least one mixed-residency layer with spare slot.
Heat threshold crossed for an eligible CPU expert and sufficient inflight capacity.
Relevant copy completion/admission differs across a boundary, and a later computation uses a changed mapping (or downstream cache history differs).
Any numerical causal chain additionally requires an actual arithmetic/state difference and propagation into routing/draft/verification/sampling; none is established here.
cases_where_this_explanation_does_not_ap: Caching disabled, all relevant experts GPU-resident, no eligible swap, or no threshold crossed.
Completions occur before the same boundaries and mappings remain identical.
Changed expert is never used before the divergent event.
Changed execution placement is bit-equivalent on the relevant inputs.

source_anchors.finding: Expert cache defaults true; --no-expert-cache disables it. Selected frozen config omits this disable, retains expert-profile and DS4_STREAM=0.

Profile is loaded once into prof/prof_load, initial experts sorted stably by heat then index; mixed CPU/GPU layers reserve a spare. Heat starts from profile counts scaled to roughly 512 hits/layer. Same seed fixes this input, not future async completion.

Queue chooses hottest recently CPU-used expert and coldest GPU expert, requires heat_in > heat_out*1.25+1 by default, spare available, no layer swap pending, global inflight<8. Consumed CPU-hit batches are not kept waiting indefinitely for admission. Timing changes readiness/capacity, which can change later admitted swaps.

Background workers pop swaps, complete GGUF H2D and optional evicted-expert D2H/RAM copy, then push ready records. The GGUF helper name swap_in_mx is not limited to MXFP4 expert quantization: it handles GGUF layouts dispatched through the same container.

At post-forward boundaries cache_tick publishes only entries currently present in ready queues; it does not wait for all inflight copies. CPU/GPU slot and pointer mappings are changed, spare rotates, inflight is released. Explicit cache_drain waits all pending swaps only at its special caller before prompt buffer borrowing (10696).

GGUF sets file_experts=true even with copied RAM experts. Therefore recent slots are disabled by the !file_experts allocation condition; do not attribute this configuration to recent-slot timing. Non-GGUF copy_open/idle-event gating (1426-1432,6895-6899) is bypassed by the earlier GGUF branch; it is not needed for the supported asynchronous-swap mechanism.

Heat increments per processed expert route and decays by processed-token counts. No wall-clock-based heat selection was found. Actual CPU/GPU execution choice depends on current slot[e], not merely aggregate counts.

CPU IQ experts use iq_cpu quant/gate_up/down and CPU weighted partial accumulation; GPU residents use device matrix paths and device combination. Different implementations and grouping exist. Their complete bit equivalence for every selected expert/input is UNKNOWN from this source review; no measured CPU-vs-GPU discrepancy is claimed.
DS4_STREAM=0 disables the separate decode PCIe compute lane. Expert-cache swap workers have their own expert_cache guard and remain eligible.
INFO expert_slots/cpu_experts are derived from per-layer allocated n_vram counts. A successful swap exchanges identities while preserving these counts, and can preserve all CPU experts in RAM.

Speculative verify forwards T=n+1 rows, and forward calls cache_tick before verification acceptance/rollback. Rollback restores ring/compressor/token position, not heat/profile/slot mappings. Checkpoint restore likewise does not reset expert-cache placement. Different draft work can consequently feed different heat/cache histories after paths differ; this is not evidence of the initial cause.

N0_N1_limits: Cold prompt row0 and first decode-round row1 are byte-identical; first 16 emitted tokens shared. This excludes a visible discrepancy in those two compared target-logit rows, not all hidden state, draft distributions, cache placement or later rounds.
Aggregate 11315 GPU/4045 CPU counters and equal profile seed hashes do not encode expert identities or their time sequence.
After emitted/draft paths diverge, different heat, sampling counters and residency can be consequences rather than the cause. Do not align later flat dump rows by ordinal.
The full frozen exact-match gate failed and remains HOLD_TOKEN_PATH_DIFFERS; all typed answers correct is a separate bounded observation.
consequence: This keeps asynchronous expert placement as a source-supported alternative hypothesis. It does not exonerate the IMMA path or identify a root cause. Together with matching printed fallback SASS it narrows claims, not acceptance. No new GPU run, tolerance, replay, instrumentation or protocol work is proposed or admitted.
